A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MoDeGPT. Their complete main texts and appendices, including algorithms, proofs, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original compression experiments on OPT and LLaMA models, including perplexity, downstream accuracy, throughput, ablations and calibration sensitivity.

after.justification: V4 retains these original experiments and adds results for LLaMA-2 70B, additional tasks, computational-budget comparisons and sparsity-allocation variants.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 replaces C_sigma^(1/2) with C_sigma in both ridge leverage scores and down-matrix reconstruction. Appendix B.11 also introduces separate MLP and MHA importance scores and weighted block-level sparsity allocation, extending v1's layer-level procedure. These change the specified computations; the PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: V4 adds evaluated COPA, LAMBADA and MMLU-ml tasks in Tables 5 and 16. This is a targeted extension of the existing English-language evaluation suite. WikiText-2, PTB, Alpaca and the previously evaluated downstream tasks remain; the 70B model addition is a model-size expansion rather than new task coverage.

E2.justification: V4 adds SLEB to the retained 7B/13B perplexity comparison and evaluates OWL as a competing sparsity-allocation strategy in Tables 5 and 27. These extend an already broad comparator set. The feature-mimic, SVD-based and semi-structured comparisons from v1 remain in v4 Tables 17–19.

E3.justification: V4 evaluates LLaMA-2 70B using eight A100 GPUs, whereas v1 only extrapolated its compression requirements. Appendix B.7 introduces approximately matched total compression-plus-fine-tuning budgets, using 5,000 Alpaca samples and adjusted fine-tuning epochs. The earlier 8,000-sample recovery experiment remains separately. V4's new '2048 characters' wording conflicts with Table 3's '2048 tokens', leaving that specific setting unresolved.

E4.justification: V4 adds substantial analyses of computational-budget fairness, OWL versus the proposed allocation, separate MLP/MHA scoring, and fixed heterogeneous module sparsities (B.7 and B.10–B.12). Layer-rank distributions and broader task-degradation analyses provide additional diagnostic evidence. V1's calibration, temperature, module-compression and high-compression analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. V4 Table 27's sparsity standard deviation describes variation across layers, not uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: V4 adds substantial results for new evaluations: Table 5 reports 70B zero-shot averages of 65.51 and 66.79 for WikiText-2 and Alpaca calibration, respectively, versus 70.02 for the dense model. Table 28 reports 2722.98 tokens/s for the new block-allocation variant versus 2490.15 for uniform module sparsity. LLM-Pruner's 13B row also changes: 20% compression perplexity becomes 6.67 instead of 14.21, and numerical results replace OOM entries. Most existing MoDeGPT scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 1, Proposition 1 and Appendix A.1 revise the Type-I reconstruction and Nyström derivation, introducing an inverse-correlation factor and squared spectral-tail terms. Appendix A.4 corrects the Lagrangian derivation. B.11 adds a weighted optimization and claimed solution in Equations 42–43. These are substantive mathematical revisions, although some Type-I expressions remain unsynchronized and Equation 43 does not generally satisfy Equation 42's weighted budget.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces v1's specific novelty claim about the first structured-pruning method with nonlinear module-level error bounds with a claim to the first module-level matrix-decomposition compression method. It separately emphasizes extending decomposition theory beyond SVD. The central training-free compression claims and headline accuracy, cost and throughput claims remain.

C2.justification: V4 adds interpretations concerning LAMBADA/MMLU sensitivity, preservation of important information, the possible importance of allocation heterogeneity, and possible overfitting from emphasizing recovery fine-tuning. These extend the results discussion without replacing its central explanations. Appendix C's intrinsic-bias and reconstruction-overfitting limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V4 supplies the eight-A100 setup for 70B experiments, explicit layer ranks and allocation temperatures for 7B/70B, and sample counts, LoRA settings and timing details for the new budget comparison. The existing software, numerical precision, matrix operations and implementation disclosures are largely retained.

R1.justification: V4 adds references for SLEB, FinerCut, LLaMA-3 quantization, COPA, LAMBADA and MMLU, and develops its comparison with the already cited OWL method. FinerCut positions the new block-allocation extension but is not experimentally benchmarked. The broader related-work framework remains substantially the same.

P1.justification: The abstract and contribution list are rewritten, Section 3.2 gains a substantial explanatory roadmap, and the experimental narrative is reorganized around scalability and performance–throughput tradeoffs. Earlier main-text comparisons move into dedicated appendix subsections. These changes substantially revise exposition and organization beyond adding scientific content.

P2.justification: V4 adds a module-characteristics table, a perplexity–throughput plot, and new experimental tables and allocation figures. V1 Figure 3 survives as v4 Figure 12; its replacement in the main text is a different visualization. Figure 4 loses its parameter-share pie chart, those shares enter a table, and existing appendix memory results are also displayed in the main text.

improvement.justification: Measured 70B results, approximately matched computational budgets, and allocation comparisons substantially strengthen claims that v1 supported mainly through smaller-model experiments and extrapolation. The corrected Type-I least-squares update also addresses an important mathematical defect. These gains outweigh localized problems: Type-I formulas are not fully synchronized, and the new block-allocation solution in Equation 43 does not generally satisfy Equation 42's weighted constraint. Those issues weaken the extension and theoretical presentation, but the evidence supporting the core method is substantially stronger.
